item.title: Judge Rules Trump Unlawfully Targeted Stanford Students Who Criticized Israel
item.description: The ruling was a win for Stanford’s student newspaper, The Stanford Daily, and it followed another court victory for students targeted by the Trump administration last year.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.category: Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (Nonprofit)
item.media:description: A lawsuit argued that student journalists had been forced to self-censor out of fear of government retaliation.

item.title: Walmart to Pay $50 Million to Settle Opioid Lawsuit, US Says
item.description: The resolution is part of an effort to hold retailers and pharmacists accountable for what the government says were their roles in the opioid epidemic.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.media:description: Walmart will pay $50 million to settle claims its pharmacies filled suspicious prescriptions for opioids, the Justice Department said.

item.title: Police Make Surprise Discovery of Stolen Statue of Olympic Gymnast Sunisa Lee
item.description: The St. Paul, Minn., police were investigating a report of gunfire when they found a bronze bust of Sunisa Lee, the gold medal Olympian, that was stolen last year.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai

item.title: George Cave, C.I.A. Agent With a Role in Iran-Contra, Dies at 97
item.description: He worked throughout the Middle East before joining a secret team that tried to obtain the release of Western hostages in Lebanon in exchange for arms sent to Iran.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: For Trump, the Iran War Is Stuck Between Combat and Genuine Peace
item.description: The war has deteriorated over the past six months into Mr. Trump’s own version of a “forever war,” with no clear goals and no end in sight.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: President Trump has been unable so far to broker an agreement to end the war on satisfactory terms.

item.title: James Roche, Embattled Air Force Secretary, Dies at 86
item.description: A former executive in the weapons industry, he led the Air Force amid reports of sexual assault at its service academy and a multibillion-dollar procurement scandal.
item.dc:creator: Trip Gabriel
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: James Roche at the Pentagon in October 2001. He was named Air Force secretary earlier that year after retiring from the Navy and working as a defense contracting executive.

item.title: Hegseth Blocks Promotions of Four Army Officers as Purge Widens
item.description: The turmoil has left a leadership vacuum in the Army at a moment when it is trying to find ways to defend troops against the threat posed by cheap drones.
item.dc:creator: Greg Jaffe, Eric Schmitt and Helene Cooper
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: In 2026, Mr. Hegseth has removed at least 45 officers, selected by boards made up of peers, from promotion lists. More than half of those officers have been female or Black.

item.title: California Sues Trump Administration Over Offshore Wind Cancellation
item.description: The state is asking a court to reverse a Trump administration agreement and reinstate a planned offshore wind farm.
item.dc:creator: Heather Knight
item.media:description: A wind farm turbine off the coast of Block Island, R.I., in 2023. California was an early adopter of wind power, but offshore wind farms have so far been developed only on the East Coast.

item.title: Milo Yiannopoulos, a Right-Wing Provocateur, Is Arrested by ICE
item.description: Mr. Yiannopoulos, a prominent early supporter of President Trump, was detained at the New Orleans airport. The Trump administration publicized his arrest and shared a mug shot.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron, Hamed Aleaziz and Ken Bensinger
item.media:description: Milo Yiannopoulos at a rally in Baltimore in 2021.

item.title: Autopsy Shows Man Killed by National Guard in Memphis Was Shot in Back
item.description: The death of the man after a confrontation with National Guard troops is under investigation. An autopsy by a medical examiner shows that he was shot in the back and declared it a homicide.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:description: An autopsy released this week shows that a man killed by National Guard members in Memphis was shot in the back.

item.title: Trump Creates a Space Academy and Honors the Artemis Astronauts
item.description: President Trump presented the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the Artemis II crew, which took a journey around the moon.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:description: President Trump referred to the astronauts, including Christina Koch, Victor Glover and Reid Wiseman, as “fearless explorers.”

item.title: For Once, a New York Jet Is Destined to Win Something
item.description: A House race in Arizona pits Jay Feely, a former Jets kicker, against Amish Shah, a former sideline doctor for the team. Jets fans in the district say it’s a welcome distraction from all the losing.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Fuller
item.media:credit: Cassidy Araiza for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jets fans watching a preseason game at a bar this month in Scottsdale, Ariz., where two former members of the franchise are running against each other for a local House seat.

item.title: Jury in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial to Resume Deliberations on Monday

item.title: A Town Council Turns to a Deck of Cards to Break a Tie
item.description: Two candidates for Town Council in Gila Bend, Ariz., finished with the same number of votes. A century-old state law mandated breaking the tie with a game of chance.
item.dc:creator: Reis Thebault
item.media:credit: Anna Watts for The New York Times
item.media:description: Patricia Riggs, the interim town clerk of Gila Bend, Ariz., declared Jesus Rubalcava the winner of the Town Council seat after a game of high-card draw with the opposing candidate, Athena Guerrero.
